title: Atomic Habits - Key Concepts
description: Master the fundamental concepts from James Clear's Atomic Habits to build better habits and break bad ones

cards.back: Making small improvements of just 1% every day leads to remarkable results over time. 1.01^365 = 37.78, while 0.99^365 = 0.03

cards.front: What are the four laws of behavior change?
cards.back: 1) Make it obvious (cue), 2) Make it attractive (craving), 3) Make it easy (response), 4) Make it satisfying (reward)
The four-step loop: Cue → Craving → Response → Reward. Habits are built by completing this loop repeatedly
A strategy that links your habit to a specific time and place using the formula: 'I will [BEHAVIOR] at [TIME] in [LOCATION]'
Linking a new habit to an existing one using the formula: 'After [CURRENT HABIT], I will [NEW HABIT]'
Designing your environment to make good habits obvious and bad habits invisible. Motivation is overrated; environment often matters more

cards.front: What is the difference between motion and action?
cards.back: Motion is planning and strategizing (doesn't produce results), while action is the behavior that delivers an outcome. You can only master the habits by actually doing them
When starting a new habit, it should take less than two minutes to do. Scale down habits until they are 'too small to fail'
Humans experience peak motivation when working on tasks that are right on the edge of their current abilities - not too hard, not too easy

cards.front: What is the difference between immediate and delayed rewards?
cards.back: Good habits have a cost in the present but provide a reward in the future. Bad habits provide immediate reward but have a cost in the future
A choice you make in the present that controls your actions in the future, making it easier to maintain good habits and harder to break them

cards.front: What is the difference between outcome-based and identity-based habits?
cards.back: Outcome-based habits focus on what you want to achieve (run a marathon), while identity-based habits focus on who you wish to become (I am a runner)
Measuring whether you performed a habit or not. It provides visual proof of your progress and is naturally satisfying
When you miss a habit once, get back on track immediately. Missing once is an accident, missing twice is the start of a new habit

cards.front: What is plateaus of latent potential?
cards.back: The frustrating time when you're working hard but not seeing results. Results often come later, as a byproduct of the work done earlier

cards.front: What is the difference between being in motion and taking action?
cards.back: Motion is when you're planning, learning, and researching but not actually doing. Action is the specific behavior that produces an outcome

cards.front: What is the most effective way to change your habits?
cards.back: Change your identity first. The goal is not to read a book, the goal is to become a reader. Your identity emerges from your habits
Pairing an action you want to do with an action you need to do. For example, listening to podcasts only while exercising

cards.front: What is the 3rd rule of behavior change?
cards.back: Make it easy. The most effective form of learning is practice, not planning. Reduce friction for good habits and increase it for bad ones

cards.front: What is the difference between automatic and manual habits?
cards.back: Automatic habits are behaviors you do without thinking (brushing teeth). Manual habits require conscious effort and eventually become automatic through repetition
